title: Tea-leaves regression gambit — scratchpad
content:
Purpose
— quick personal scratchpad to capture an odd regression pattern I keep seeing in small-batch checks. Not a formal postmortem; just notes to triage, hypotheses, and lightweight rubric for spot checks.

What triggered this
— ran a 1000-sample smoke against customer prompt set (mix of instruction-following + long-context retrieval) after rolling q4_0 quantized builds to staging (build v2026.02.10 -> v2026.03.01). Noticed: nasty repetitive token loops on ~2% of long-context (>=1200 tokens) samples. Previously ~0.2%.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked)
1) Quantization-induced KV-cache temperature mismatch: kv cache keys/values drifting -> attention focusing on a tiny token window -> repetition.
2) Batching heuristic change in v2026.03.01: longer accumulation window -> weird prefix alignment with cache.
3) Tokenizer mismatch at boundaries for certain unicode sequences -> off-by-one leading to guard token repetition.
4) Different fallback model routing for heavy requests (was hitting cpu-fallback path intermittently).

Immediate reproduction steps (workable)
- Use sample id set: SAMPLE-REG-0001..00050 from the customer mix (I've attached a local csv in the private run, not in this doc).
- Run with: model=redwood-13b-q4_0 / batch_size=1 / kv_cache=true / max_length=2048 / stream=false
- Toggle: quantized=false (float16) and compare.

Observed signals (raw)
- Failure mode: repeating 3–6 token n-grams starting ~ token 1600. Repeats until max_length or stop token.
- Token counts: mean tokens before repeat (quantized) = 1580; (float16) = 1840 (so quantized shorter generation sometimes)
- Latency delta: quantized path slightly faster (expected) but tail-latency variance up by 12% on repeating runs.

Ad-hoc rubric for quick triage (0–3) — use when spot-checking sample set
- Instruction following (0: fails to follow, 3: precise)
- Coherence (0: repeats / incoherent, 3: sustained coherence)
- Hallucination (0: invents facts blatantly, 3: grounded)
- Stability (0: generates long loop, 3: clean stop)
- Severity summary: color: green/yellow/red based on avg <=1.0 red, <=2.0 yellow, >2 green.

Pair of annotated examples (from sample set)
--- sample A (prompt excerpt) ---
Prompt: "You are a notes assistant. Summarize the meeting minutes and extract action items. Context: ... long blob (omitted) ..."
Quantized (v2026.03.01) output: "Action items: 1. Follow up with legal. 2. Schedule sync next week. 2. Schedule sync next week. 2. Schedule sync next week. 2. Schedule sync next week."
Rubric scores: Instruction following 2, Coherence 1, Hallucination 2, Stability 0

Float16 (v2026.02.10) output: "Action items: 1. Follow up with legal. 2. Schedule sync next week. 3. Circulate slide deck."
Rubric scores: Instruction following 3, Coherence 3, Hallucination 3, Stability 3

Notes on the example: repetition starts after the first list completed; quantized run seems to glue the last list token and loop.

Quick experiments plan (one-liners)
- Re-run sample A with kv_cache=false (to check cache behavior).
- Re-run at batch_size=1 and batch_size=4 to see batching effect.
- Run with prefix-padding disabled (weirdness sometimes with pack/unpack).
- Try alternate tokenizer variant (v2) for boundary edge cases.

Slack thread / tickets I pinged
- pinged #runtime-latency (Noah) re: tail latency change — thread id above
- opened RL-2147: "q4_0 small-batch repetition regression" (assigned to Mira)
- PR linked: github PR 812: microbatched buffer alignment change — suspicious

Open questions (unresolved)
- Is the repeat exclusively on long contexts, or is it more correlated to prompt content shape (lists, numbered bullets)? Need A/B on content shape.
- Does RBAC/pinning cause occasional fallback to CPU path? logs unclear.
- Is the tokenizer off-by-one happening only with certain unicode sequences? I saw 3 samples with emojis around token boundary.

Operational checks to add to console (nice-to-have)
- Add histogram: tokens-before-repeat for each build and quantization profile (per-model).
- Add sample-level fingerprint (prompt hash) to the trace to group repeats.
- Expose kv_cache hit/miss ratio in trace view.

Decisions / next steps (me + Mira)
- Today: run the 50-sample focused experiment matrix (kv on/off, quant on/off, batch 1/4) and log outputs to /tmp/regression-run-03.
- If repeat reproduces with kv_cache=false -> deprioritize cache theory. If persists only with quantized -> escalate to model-quant team.
- If batching shows correlation -> revert batching heuristics in PR-812 for canary.

Loose notes / mental TODOs
- Consider small deterministic perturbation to stop token probability when long sequences approach max_length (cheap guard).
- Talk to Mira about adding a tiny randomized early-stop during canary to avoid user-visible worst-case loops.

Scratch log (timestamps)
- 2026-03-10 09:30: initial run -> noticed spike in repeats (~2% -> flagged)
- 2026-03-10 10:05: quick AB on float16 vs q4_0 -> reproduces on quantized
- 2026-03-10 11:20: raised RL-2147 and pinged Noah
- 2026-03-11 14:40: looked into PR-812 diffs (batching alignment changes) -> flagged as suspect

Final quick heuristics to apply when triaging future regressions
- Always collect: prompt hash, tokenized length, model build id, quant/profile, batch size, kv_cache flag, runtime path (gpu/cpu fallback), seed
- If repetition rate > 1% on same seed + model config -> escalate immediately (ticket + triage channel)

Random scribbles at bottom — things to ask the model team later
- How deterministic is q4_0 across restarts when using the same seed?
- Are there any known rounding changes in kernel selection between builds?

End of scratchpad.

(If this becomes a postmortem, reorder into timeline + root cause + mitigations; for now this is a rapid capture.)
